title: India Launches 'Friends of MY Bharat' to Connect Diaspora Youth With Nation-Building Efforts
excerpt: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has launched a new initiative under the MY Bharat platform aimed at engaging Indian-origin youth across the world with India's development journey.
body:
• The 'Friends of MY Bharat' initiative targets Indian-origin youth living abroad, creating a formal channel to participate in India's development programs
  • The initiative builds on the MY Bharat platform, which has registered over 2 crore youth and generated more than 1.5 lakh volunteering opportunities since its 2023 launch
  • The program aligns with India's broader diaspora engagement strategy, including the Know India Program and the Viksit Bharat Run held across 100+ countries

India's Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has launched 'Friends of MY Bharat,' a new initiative designed to connect Indian-origin youth living abroad with India's development priorities and volunteer opportunities.

The program extends the reach of the existing Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) platform — India's largest youth engagement infrastructure — beyond domestic borders to engage the global Indian diaspora. It represents the Indian government's latest effort to formalize the participation of second-generation and overseas Indian youth in the country's development trajectory.

Building on MY Bharat's Domestic Scale

MY Bharat was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 31, 2023, as a technology-driven platform connecting Indian youth aged 15-29 with government programs, volunteering, experiential learning, and skill-building opportunities. The platform has since registered over 2.15 crore youth and 1.2 lakh organizations, generating more than 1.52 lakh volunteering opportunities across sectors including health, education, environment, disaster response, and community service, according to government data.

The platform recorded a Guinness World Record on June 4, 2026, when 390,812 verified participants joined an online quiz within a single week. Its mobile application, available in 22 Indian languages, has been downloaded more than 100,000 times since its October 2025 launch.

The 'Friends of MY Bharat' initiative now extends this engagement framework to the estimated 32 million-strong Indian diaspora, with a particular focus on youth who may want to contribute to India's growth story from abroad.

Part of a Broader Diaspora Strategy

The initiative fits into a broader pattern of Indian government programs designed to strengthen ties with the global Indian community. The Know India Program, now in its 88th edition, brings young diaspora professionals aged 24-28 to India for two-week immersive experiences covering governance, technology, and cultural heritage. The 88th edition runs from August 16-29, 2026.

Last year, the Viksit Bharat Run 2025 saw Indian diaspora members participate in community runs across more than 100 countries and 150 international cities — from Sydney to San Francisco — as part of the government's Seva Pakhwada initiative. Participants took the Viksit Bharat Pledge and connected with the MY Bharat portal.

"When the strength of the country's youth is involved in nation-building, it is of immense help. MY Bharat is playing a major role in fulfilling this responsibility."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi

What It Means for NRI Families

For Indian-origin families in the US, UK, Canada, and other diaspora hubs, the initiative creates a structured pathway for their children to engage with India beyond annual visits and cultural events. The MY Bharat platform's experiential learning programs, civic engagement quizzes, and volunteering tracks could offer young NRIs a way to build meaningful connections with their ancestral country.

The planned MY Bharat 2.0 upgrade will incorporate artificial intelligence, multilingual technologies, and open APIs to support participation from outside India. The government's long-term objective is to engage more than 100 million young people through the platform as part of the Viksit Bharat@2047 vision.

Details on specific enrollment pathways and programs available to diaspora youth are expected to be published on the MY Bharat portal at mybharat.gov.in.
